outcome: Pregnancy-related complications (preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, placenta complications)
cohort: 2,930 pregnancies to women with multiple sclerosis (MS) compared with 56,958 pregnancies in the general population in Denmark
finding: While there were no differences in severe adverse perinatal outcomes between women with MS and the general population, women with MS had a higher prevalence of elective c-sections, induced delivery, and infants born SGA, but a lower prevalence of asphyxia.
mod_finding: Elective caesarean section was more common in the study cohort (women with MS).
